title: Quishing Challenge
description: QR phishing is 11% of phishing in 2024 -- can you spot a tampered QR?

questions.q: Why does QR phishing bypass many email gateways?
options: QR images hide the URL from link scanners
QR codes are too small to scan
questions.explanation: Gateways scan visible links. A QR in a PNG/PDF hides the URL in an image -- Barracuda found 500k such emails in 3 months. The link is only revealed after you scan with a phone outside corporate protection.

questions.q: SCENARIO: Email from HR with a QR in a PDF: Scan to view benefits update. No link, just a QR. You were not expecting it. Safest action?
options: Open PDF on laptop then scan
Verify via HR portal or call HR on known number, don't scan
Forward to personal email to scan safely
questions.explanation: QR in PDFs is a classic quishing pattern (Barracuda). Verify via a known channel; don't scan unsolicited QR. Forwarding spreads the image.

questions.q: A QR code stuck on top of a real parking meter QR (with tape residue) is likely safe if the URL preview shows HTTPS.
questions.explanation: False. Overlay is a prime tamper sign (Houston parking). Even HTTPS can be phishing -- the domain matters, not just the padlock. Don't scan overlayed codes.

questions.q: 27% of QR attacks fake which scenario?
questions.explanation: Abnormal AI: 27% of QR attacks fake MFA setup ('scan to enable MFA'). The urgency (lose access) drives scans. Real MFA setup is initiated by you, not via random QR.

questions.q: SCENARIO: You scan a menu QR and it asks for camera, contacts, and location before showing the menu. What do you do?
options: Deny and find a menu or type the restaurant's official site
questions.explanation: Excessive permissions is a red flag. A menu needs no contacts. Deny and use the official site or ask staff.

questions.q: Best preview habit before tapping a QR link?
options: Use native camera preview, verify domain is expected and not misspelled (arnazon vs amazon)
questions.explanation: Native camera shows the URL. Check for misspellings, long random paths, or non-HTTPS on login pages. Third-party apps may violate privacy.

questions.q: Real-time QR analysis that extracts and crawls the link can block ~1.5M daily quishing attempts (Microsoft).
questions.explanation: True. Inline sandbox + computer vision to decode QR in images/PDFs is how modern email security now catches quishing before delivery.

questions.q: SCENARIO: You scanned a QR, entered your Microsoft password, then realized the domain was microsft-login.com. First step?
options: Change that password immediately + enable 2FA + revoke sessions
questions.explanation: Stolen creds are used within minutes. Change now, enable MFA, revoke sessions/tokens, and report. Don't wait.

title: Deepfake & Voice Clone Defense
description: AI voices fooled 80% of listeners -- test your resistance to deepfake vishing.

questions.q: Modern AI needs at least 5 minutes of audio to clone a voice.
questions.explanation: False. Group-IB: 3 seconds can suffice via ElevenLabs/Tacotron2. That's why a brief 'Hello?' can be enough -- limit public voice samples.

questions.q: SCENARIO: Hi, its Dad, I'm in jail, need bail, don't tell Mom, wire now -- voice sounds like Dad, number is Dad's. Best action?
options: Wire immediately -- urgency + familiar voice + caller ID all match
Call Dad back on his known number and use your family code word
Ask the caller to prove by describing yesterday's dinner
Text Dad at the same number to confirm
questions.explanation: All three signals (voice, number, urgency) can be spoofed. CISA: use a pre-agreed code word + call back on a known number via a separate channel.

questions.q: Which defence is NOT effective against deepfake vishing?
questions.explanation: Voice-only approval is what attackers exploit. STIR/SHAKEN helps, but not universally. Require 2-channel approval.

questions.q: SCENARIO: CFO (voice cloned) asks finance to wire 50k to 'new vendor account' and says 'Keep this between us.' Team is busy. Your move?
options: Check email for approval then wire
Follow dual-approval: verify via known CFO number + vendor portal, despite urgency
Ask the caller to send a voice note
questions.explanation: Urgency + secrecy + authority = BEC/deepfake signature. Mandiant test: busy teams bypassed Edge/SmartScreen under urgency. Follow process, not voice.

questions.q: Real-time voice cloning (attacker speaks live, you hear cloned voice) is still theoretical and not yet feasible.
questions.explanation: False. NCC Group demonstrated real-time voice conversion routing mic -> ML model -> Teams/Meet live. Delay is now low enough to be convincing.

questions.q: What percentage of ViKing AI vishing bots succeeded when participants were not warned?
questions.explanation: ViKing study (240 participants): 77% disclosed when not warned, 52% overall, still 33% when strongly warned -- awareness helps but isn't sufficient; need technical controls.

questions.q: SCENARIO: You receive a Teams call that looks like your CEO, video is slightly off but voice is perfect, asking to reset a password post-breach. Action?
options: End call, call CEO back on known number, verify via IT ticket
Ask CEO to turn on camera
questions.explanation: Video can also be deepfaked (NCC is working on syncing audio/video). Always verify via a separate, trusted channel before privileged actions.

questions.q: Best long-term reduction of voice exposure?
options: Post more videos to prove real voice
Limit executive voice online: private LinkedIn/YouTube, no voicemail with full name
Use voicemail with full name for trust
Share voice samples publicly to claim ownership
questions.explanation: Reduce harvestable audio. NCC: executives' public voice is the source. Private settings + no full-name voicemail reduces cloning material.

title: BEC Simulation Lab
description: Sniper fraud: $2.9B in 2023. Spot the subtle thread hijack.

questions.q: SCENARIO: Thread with vendor L.E.K. Consulting -- From: accounts@lekconsultancy.com (registered 21h ago), Reply-To: admin@abpllty.cc (4 months old). DMARC pass (SPF only, no DKIM). CEO 'approves' in quote. Action?
options: Pay -- CEO approved and DMARC passed
Treat as BEC: DMARC pass on SPF alone is useless for identity; verify From vs Reply-To vs vendor via known portal
questions.explanation: Ironscales: DMARC pass on SPF alone says the envelope domain authorises the relay, not that the CEO wrote it. Multiple identities + new domain = BEC. Verify outside email.

questions.q: Median BEC loss per Verizon DBIR that makes it dangerous?
questions.explanation: $50k -- small enough to clear without escalation, hence success. Not 'too small to matter' -- it's designed to be.

questions.q: SCENARIO: Finance gets 'Update remittance to new account' inside a real thread with a real vendor. The only change is one digit in the account. Best check?
options: Reply to thread asking 'Is this correct?'
Call vendor on number on file (not signature) and use vendor portal
questions.explanation: Conversation hijacking: attacker lurks, then edits one line. Call on file + portal change, not email signature which attacker controls.

questions.q: BEC always contains a malicious link or attachment to scan.
questions.explanation: False. Many BECs are pure text (no payload) -- that's why payload scanners miss them. Detection is relationship + language.

questions.q: SCENARIO: Houston doggy daycare got invoice on correct letterhead with 'construction' misspelled as 'construciton' in email. Two prior correct wires succeeded. Next step?
options: Wire -- letterhead + prior success proves it
Inspect sender domain letter-by-letter, call construction on known number, confirm via portal
questions.explanation: Letterhead and prior success are trust anchors attackers exploit. One-letter swap is the tell. Verify out-of-band.

questions.q: Which BEC type uses AI to clone voice + display name + urgency?
questions.explanation: Hybrid BEC + deepfake vishing: AI voice + spoofed ID + urgency. Devices can't verify voice alone.

questions.q: SCENARIO: You are accounts payable and see a vendor change after 2 years of same details. Policy says dual-approval. Boss says 'Skip it, we're late.' You?
options: Enforce policy: dual-approval anyway, document refusal
Ask vendor via email if change is real
questions.explanation: Policy exists for this exact pressure scenario. Enforce and document. The boss's voice/email could itself be spoofed.

questions.q: FBI IC3 2023 BEC losses were ~$2.9B from ~21k reports.
questions.explanation: True. High loss per report shows targeted, high-value nature vs. mass phishing.

title: Nigeria Smishing Lab
description: BVN, NIN, OTP -- Nigeria-specific traps, from fake alerts to job bait.

questions.q: SCENARIO: SMS: Your BVN has been blocked. Re-validate: http://nimc-verify.tk/update to avoid deactivation. Your BVN is fine. Action?
options: Delete -- NIMC never asks to re-validate via SMS link; check via *456* or NIMC portal
questions.explanation: BVN/NIN blocked is classic smishing. NIMC uses nimc.gov.ng, not .tk. Verify via official short code/portal, never via link.

questions.q: Which token will a legitimate Nigerian bank NEVER ask for via phone/SMS?
questions.explanation: Banks, telcos, and NIMC never ask for OTP/PIN/BVN/NIN via call/SMS. Any such request = vishing/smishing.

questions.q: SCENARIO: Call: This is your bank, we're reversing a debit, read the OTP we just sent. The OTP arrives from your bank's short code. You?
options: Read it -- the code is from your bank
Hang up, call bank on known number -- the code was triggered by the attacker
Ask caller for staff ID then read
questions.explanation: The attacker initiated the transaction, causing the bank to send you a real OTP. Reading it completes their transfer. Hang up + call back.

questions.q: Job SMS: You have been shortlisted for work-from-home, earn 50k daily, pay 5k processing fee. This is:
questions.explanation: Advance-fee job scam: fee for kit/training, then disappearance. Real employers never charge fees and don't interview only via chat.

questions.q: A text with a link to 'opay-verify.tk' is likely legitimate because it contains 'opay.'
questions.explanation: False. Brand in subdomain/path is not the brand. Real OPay is opayweb.com. 'opay-verify.tk' wraps the brand in a disposable .tk.

questions.q: SCENARIO: Your line will be barred in 24hrs. Click to link NIN: http://airtel.link-nin.ng -- you already linked. What check?
options: Check via *996# or official Airtel app, ignore link
questions.explanation: SIM-barring pressure is smishing. Verify via USSD/app you already have, not the link. Check sender vs real Airtel (airtel.com.ng).

questions.q: What makes BVN/NIN solicitation 'anomalous by definition'?
options: They are secret and banks ask often
No legitimate institution asks for them via unsolicited message
questions.explanation: Concentration of Nigerian fraud around BVN/NIN/OTP means any unsolicited request for them is almost certainly phishing -- strong local signal.

title: Incident Response Simulation
description: You clicked. Now contain it -- fast.

questions.q: SCENARIO: You entered your password on a fake Microsoft login 2 minutes ago. What is the FIRST action (seconds matter)?
options: Wait to see if email arrives
Change that password now + revoke sessions + enable 2FA, and do same anywhere reused
questions.explanation: Stolen creds are used within minutes by bots. Change + revoke + 2FA closes the window fastest. Antivirus is next, not first.

questions.q: You opened a PDF with a QR that you suspect was quishing. You did NOT enter data. Next step?
options: Close tab, clear cache, run AV, report to SOC/helpdesk with headers
Forward PDF to colleagues to check
questions.explanation: Even without data entry, malware could have loaded. Close, clear, scan, and report with headers. Don't forward payload.

questions.q: SCENARIO: Finance just wired 50k to a new account (BEC). It's been 10 minutes. Best containment?
options: Call bank to recall + contact SOC + preserve headers -- speed is critical
Wait for vendor to confirm receipt
questions.explanation: Wire recall window is minutes before mule laundering. Call bank + SOC now. Email is too slow and may go to attacker.

questions.q: Staying silent after clicking is better than reporting because you'll get in trouble.
questions.explanation: False. Silence turns a near-miss into a breach. Fast reporting lets SOC contain; culture should reward reporters.

questions.q: SCENARIO: Your phone shows an MFA push you didn't trigger. You should:
options: Deny, change password now, check sessions
questions.explanation: MFA fatigue: attacker has your password and spams pushes hoping you'll approve to stop noise. Deny + change.

questions.q: After a breach, which backup is safest to restore from?
options: USB that was connected during attack
questions.explanation: Ransomware hunts connected drives. Offline/versioned cloud survives. Test restores quarterly.

questions.q: You should try to 'investigate' the phishing link yourself in a private window.
questions.explanation: False. Don't investigate -- you may trigger drive-by or tip off attacker. Report with headers and let SOC sandbox it.
